ICS: Learner should greet Mary to start encounter.
Learner should assess understanding, e.g. “Tell me in your own words what you heard last time we spoke so we can continue the conversation.”

Learner might pick up on the fact that it sounds like Mary’s friend may have been on a phase I or II trial, not phase III; regardless, the learner should start with background information about trials, and then specify background details for this particular trial.
Learner should explain bias as the basis for randomization.
Learner should explain stopping trial early for crossover and a monitoring committee.
Learner should introduce equipoise, acknowledging that most people would want to be on the intervention arm of the study.

The learner should have the handout about Miraculin and can show Mary, if he/she hasn’t already, and can discuss that there is patient information about the study and the drugs including side effects.
Finally, the learner should discuss that there is a consent form that Mary can take home along with the patient information to look over and no signature is required at this time.
